note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. DC quirk: in the overwhelmingly Democratic District, the June 16, 2026 primary (the city's first using ranked choice voting) effectively decides both races; the general is November 3.

DC-house-at-large.statusNote: Open seat: Del. Eleanor Holmes Norton, 89, in office since 1991, ended her re-election bid on January 25, 2026. At-large Councilmember Robert White (D) won the June 16 Democratic primary with 63% over Councilmember Brooke Pinto (22%); he faces Denise Rosado (R), Kymone Freeman (Statehood Green), and David Solana (I) in November. In deep-blue DC the primary winner is the de facto winner.

DC-mayor.statusNote: Open seat: Mayor Muriel Bowser announced November 25, 2025 she would not seek a fourth term. Ward 4 Councilmember Janeese Lewis George (D), a democratic socialist, won the June 16 Democratic primary with 54% of first-choice votes over Kenyan McDuffie (36%); the primary effectively decides the race. Also certified for November: Robert L. Gross (Statehood Green), plus 13 independent or minor candidates including Rhonda Hamilton (I); the other 12 independents drew no substantive coverage and are not curated here. No Republican qualified.

candidates.name: Robert White
candidates.background: Fifth-generation Washingtonian and at-large DC councilmember since 2016; earlier spent five years as legislative counsel to Del. Eleanor Holmes Norton. Ran second to Bowser in the 2022 mayoral primary. Won the June 16, 2026 Democratic primary for the open delegate seat with 63% over Brooke Pinto (22%).
priorities: DC statehood and defending Home Rule
Make DC affordable for working people
Good-paying jobs and youth-focused crime prevention

cost.label: Advocated 'legislation to force employers to provide 12 weeks of paid sick leave'; campaign centers on lowering household costs (Wikipedia)

housing.label: 'Stronger federal investment in affordable housing production, preservation of existing affordable units, rehabilitation of neglected public housing', alongside increasing housing production (WTOP)

immigration.label: Pledges to protect DC residents 'from ICE and unaccountable federal agents' (campaign site)

climate.label: Sponsored the Renewable Energy Future Amendment Act on the DC Council; endorsed by Sierra Club DC (Wikipedia)

education.label: Wrote the Birth to Three for All DC Act expanding early childhood education and child care subsidies (Wikipedia)

safety.label: 'Fully staffing our courts, supporting accountable, effective policing, and investing in violence prevention and youth opportunity'; invest to 'prevent crime before it starts' (WTOP)

controversies.label: In 2019 reversed his opposition to DC's no-bid $215M sports-betting contract after his committee gained new oversight authority, and took a $2,000 donation from an executive of a contractor facing whistleblower allegations despite an earlier no-corporate-money pledge (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Denise Rosado
candidates.background: Lawyer and former federal attorney advisor, bilingual in English and Spanish. Ran unopposed for the June 16, 2026 Republican nomination for delegate; first Republican general-election contender for the seat since Norton's retirement opened it.
priorities: Revitalize downtown and expand housing supply
Federal income-tax exemption for DC residents

housing.label: 'If you increase the supply of housing, it will reduce demand, making housing more affordable': convert vacant properties, cut bureaucratic barriers to attract private developers, while also backing 'new investment' in affordable housing (campaign platform)

safety.label: Calls for 'smarter, tougher public safety policy' and continued coordination with federal law enforcement (campaign site)

democracy.label: 'DC cannot become a state under the Constitution as it is currently written'; says statehood requires a constitutional amendment and pushes tax exemption instead (campaign platform)

candidates.name: Kymone Freeman
candidates.background: Playwright, community activist, and co-founder of We Act Radio, a progressive station on Martin Luther King Jr. Avenue in Southeast DC. Ran against Norton in 2024 as the DC Statehood Green nominee (7%) and is again the party's nominee in 2026, campaigning under the banner 'No Representation, No Taxes'.
priorities: Federal tax resistance until DC has representation
Addressing root causes of violence and inequality

housing.label: Would mandate that HUD designate '30% of a person's income as the maximum monthly rent' (Washington Informer)

safety.label: Wants to address 'root causes of violence' through holistic solutions, citing systemic resource gaps like Ward 3 having three times more grocery stores than Ward 7 (Washington Informer)

democracy.label: Statehood advocate who backed Initiative 83's ranked choice voting and open primaries, opposing the 'closed primary system as a tool to silence D.C.'s growing non-party affiliated population' (Green Party US)

candidates.name: Janeese Lewis George
candidates.background: Third-generation Washingtonian, Howard Law graduate, and former juvenile prosecutor in the DC attorney general's office; Ward 4 councilmember since 2021 and a self-described democratic socialist. Won the June 16, 2026 Democratic primary for the open mayor's seat with 54% of first-choice votes over Kenyan McDuffie (36%) in DC's first ranked-choice election.
priorities: Universal childcare capped at 7% of household income
Publicly owned social housing and 72,000 new homes
Standing up to federal intervention in DC

cost.label: Universal childcare: 'every family will be eligible for childcare assistance and will spend no more than 7% of their household income on childcare' (campaign platform)

housing.label: 'Dignified Homes DC, a bold commitment to build publicly owned, mixed-income housing' plus 'strengthen and expand DC's rent stabilization program', while also pledging to 'reform zoning laws, streamline the permitting process' (campaign platform)

immigration.label: Would start by 'rescinding the MPD order that permits our officers to work with ICE, sharing information and transferring people to ICE custody' (campaign platform)

taxes.label: Backs a Business Activity Tax on law and lobbying firms worth 'an additional $500 million': 'I would not raise taxes on working families or middle class residents' (NOTUS interview)

education.label: 'Expand after-school programming in all eight Wards', school-based mental health, special education services, and 'expand the workforce at schools' (campaign platform)

safety.label: 'Comprehensive public safety strategy that addresses prevention, intervention, and enforcement' built on Community Hubs linking families to jobs and mental health services (campaign platform)

democracy.label: Will 'walk the halls of Congress herself' toward 'protecting DC autonomy and passing DC Statehood'; pledges to protect Home Rule against federal overreach (campaign platform)

candidates.name: Robert Gross
candidates.background: Washington native and military veteran who worked on aircraft before roughly a decade in information technology; attended Cardozo Education Campus. The youngest candidate in the race, running as the DC Statehood Green Party nominee on a platform of modernizing DC government with AI and closing east-of-the-river investment gaps.
priorities: Modernize DC government operations with AI
Close economic gaps east of the Anacostia River

housing.label: Proposes the District Housing Utilization and Family Stability Act creating differentiated housing vouchers, with new construction meeting a 'Green Housing Modernization Standard'; would also streamline housing-development approvals (Green Party US)

climate.label: Climate resiliency agenda: clean public transportation, green infrastructure, energy-efficient buildings, and expanding the urban tree canopy (Green Party US)

candidates.name: Rhonda Hamilton
candidates.now: Founder and director, M.I. Mother's Keep (mental health nonprofit)
candidates.background: Mental health advocate and small business owner who founded the nonprofit M.I.
